turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So what brings you into the family clinic today?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I've had this sore throat for the past three days and it doesn't seem to be getting any better at all. I feel sort of feverish so. I just thought I should come in and get this checked out.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when did you start having this sore throat?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Three days ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about the fever?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: The fever I noticed maybe a day back.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and did you get any temperature measurements?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I didn't take any myself. But I felt hot, and I felt chills.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have your sore throat or fever gone worse at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think it's getting worse, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And does it usually happen during the day, throughout the night or does it have any sort of pattern?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say that it doesn't really have a pattern. The sore throat is always there and the fever started a day back and it seems to break sometimes, but right now there is no real pattern to it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And besides that, do you have any cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no cough.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you tried anything that has helped you at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I tried just like those Lozenges and seems to be helping just soothe my throat, but it's a temporary relief.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you had anything like this happen to you before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like this.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And is the sore throat constant? Or does it come and go?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say it's pretty constant now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you been around anyone that has been sick recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not that I know of.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Anything that makes your sore throat worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I guess swallowing foods makes it worse, or at least it's painful.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you at all noticed any like swelling around your neck region, like swelling of your lymph nodes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So yeah, not swelling of my entire neck, but I have felt some lumps in my neck.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about any swelling anywhere else on your body?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nowhere else.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you noticed any kind of skin changes like rashes or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you traveled at all recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nowhere.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you have any headaches or nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and any night sweats.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you feel fatigued like increased tiredness at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Umm, yeah, I've been feeling really tired.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any chest pain or feeling that your heart is racing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any issues with bowel movements, like any diarrhea or constipation? P No, no, that's been normal. OK, any changes in your urination?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no changes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you been getting sleep at night or do you have to keep waking up?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I've been getting OK, I sleep like, I've been sleeping about 7 to 8 hours.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And how about your appetite?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say that's been OK as well, it's just hard to eat a lot of food because of this sore throat.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And is it just with solids or do you get the soreness with liquids too?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say mostly with solids, sometimes with liquid. If it's like really cold or something.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Do you have any kind of allergies to anything in your house like carpets, pets or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you had any recent infections like a cold?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK. And do you have any past medical conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I have Crohn's disease.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And when did you get diagnosed with Crohn's?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: That would have been last year.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Last year, OK. And are you taking any medications for your Crohn's disease?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I am on something for it, I think it's Sulfasalazine or something like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And any other medications besides that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any previous hospitalizations or surgeries?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I had a colonoscopy done. I just needed hospitalization for just the day I guess.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and when was that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: That was also last year.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Last year, OK. And do you have any family history of any conditions that run in the family? Like do you have any Crohn's disease or Ulcerative Colitis that run in the family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, both do.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Both do, OK. Any anything else that runs in the family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I know there's some asthma and eczema that run in the family too.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And you mentioned you haven't been around anyone that was sick or recently got sick?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And where do you currently live?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I live in an apartment by myself. Sorry, not by myself, with my parents and my younger brother.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you at all drink alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I drank once or twice in the past, but I didn't like it. It makes my Crohn's worse so I stay away from it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you smoke cigarettes?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And how about any other drugs like marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright, so do you partake in any like sports or activities or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, I swim.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any contact sports?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Alright, so yeah, overall it seems that you had this sore throat which is constant, getting worse and a bit of a fever in th last one or two days and you've also had swelling in your neck and so yeah, do you have any other questions or concerns?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, like what do you think I have? Do you think it's COVID?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, so definitely at this time, you know whenever people have any respiratory symptoms we always want to rule out COVID.  So will definitely get a swab for COVID testing done for you today which should come back within 24 to 48 hours and in the meantime you should self isolate. And other than that, it can also be, due to this swelling in your lymph nodes and also just the other symptoms, it can be other viral infections. It can be mono so we definitely have to do a couple of tests, and there's one test that will do for mono as well which is called EBV antibody testing. So we'll do a couple of these tests today and then see what what comes back. And in the meantime you should definitely self isolate if you haven't been doing so already.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK, sure I can do that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, do you have any questions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, that sounds good. Thank you so much.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: You're welcome. Take care.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: You too.
